He made a bad decision to pull out of the draft last year and to stay in it this year.  If he develops, he could be a steal.  But his body is several years away.

picks.tradeNote: from DEN via MIN, PHX, CHA, and PHX

analysis.text: He has great size and is very skilled for the position.  According to scouts, he's more athletic than Kosta Perovic and a bit more polished in the post.  Good hands.  Can play with his back to the basket.
Needs to get stronger.  At 7-foot-1, 240 he could use another 20 pounds of muscle before playing in the post.  Despite his size, he isn't a great rebounder.

Ilic declared for the 2004 NBA draft but withdrew when he wasn't guaranteed to be a first-round pick.  Averaged 7.3 ppg and 3.5 rpg this season. He's spent the past few years playing for BC Reflex in Serbia and is one of the better big man prospects in the draft.  He's represented by Darko Milicic's agent, Marc Cornstein.
No. 22 to 30 overall

Surprised everyone by leaving his name in the draft. Nuggets and Heat both walked away impressed after a recent dominating performance in the Serbia playoffs. He's very skilled, but a little on the soft side.

After scoring a big hit with Nenad Krstic a few years ago, the Nets go international again. Ilic is a true center who has really come on of late in Serbia.  He's very skilled, but he will need to bulk up to play center in the pros.  It may be another year or two before he joins the Nets full-time.

One of the best young rebounders in Europe.  He's long, bouncy and relentless on the glass.  He's quite quick for his size and plays very physical for a European.   He has a great motor and is one of the hardest working players in the Euroleague.  He also is an excellent defender.

He's not very skilled.  Offensively, he gets almost all of his points on put backs.  He doesn't have much of a perimeter game at all.   He also doesn't do a lot  with the ball around the basket.  He has few low post moves to really speak about.
Averaged 7.4 ppg and 4.2 rpg in 18.9 mpg  for Real Madrid this season.  In 2003, was the leading rebounder in the ULEB league.  Is draft eligible this year.
Second round

Scouts love how hard Hervelle works and think he has the size, athleticism and toughness to be a decent rotation player in the league.  However, comparing him to a Euro Dennis Rodman is a bit much considering he averaged just 4 rpg this season.

The Nuggets spent a lot of time overseas and know what they're doing.  Hervelle is considered one of the best rebounders in Europe.  He's long, athletic and relentless on the boards.  His defense is way ahead of his offense at this point, but in a few years he could be another Anderson Varejao type of energy player in the paint.

picks.tradeNote: from DET via NYK, BKN, PHX, ORL and LAC

analysis.text: Skilled big man with a great feel for the game.  Can score with either hand in the low post.  Has a soft jumper that he can hit from just about anywhere.  Possess a nice handle and sees the floor very well for a big man.  Has been in huge in several key games for Climano this season.

Not a great athlete.  Lacks lateral quickness or any type of vertical leaping ability.  Is a below average defender, especially when playing against long, athletic big men. Disappears sometimes and has developed a reputation for being a little soft.

Averaged 9.2 ppg and 4.9 rpg in the Euroleague for Climano Bologna this year. Had a 24-point, seven-rebound game versus Zalgris in the Euroleague Top 16. Was a top prospect in Europe before a lackluster year at Michigan State sent his stock plummeting. Declared for the draft last year, but pulled out when he couldn't get a promise in the first round. Has declared for the draft again this year and will stay in.
Second round

As far as skills and experience go, he's a great prospect.  But his lack of NBA athleticism along with his defensive inadequacies probably mean he's a second-round pick no matter how much more he develops over in Europe.

Lorbek is one of the best player in Europe right now.  He's big and skilled and he has been getting major experience in the Euroleague.  His lack of athleticism may hold him back from being a successful NBA player.
A young, intriguing point guard from Turkey who just turned 18 this year.  Obviously this is a long-term pick for the Hawks.

picks.tradeNote: from OKC via SA and MIA

analysis.text: Good athlete with good size for his position.  Good defender.  Excellent at getting into the lane and drawing fouls.  Good free throw shooter.
Struggles with the jumper.
Second Round

After David Lee and Luther Head, Anderson was the best player at the Chicago pre-draft camp. Anderson's athleticism, strength and ability to get into the lane and draw fouls impressed just about everyone. His 18 points on the last day put him over the top as the best scorer in the camp. If his jump shot were a little better, he'd get consideration in the first round.
